svg.aria-label: Scenario 1, the whole thesis, run end to end from your session. You ask: Run my thesis end to end. In your session, step 1: /research-master:conductor runs the pipeline from your session; it reads the tracker and the overlay's stage order and sends each stage to whoever does that work; it never does substantive work, skips a MANDATORY stop or overrides a HARD-STOP. Step 2, across the context boundary: dispatch the stage to its role, workflow or script, carrying spec, hash and brief path: the full role spec, the RULES_HASH line, the return format and the inputs that role's input contract allows, for a drafting or check stage the brief by path; blind-reviewer gets only the bundle from tools/anonymize.py and the venue, never the brief, the overlay or the tracker; sparring-partner gets the proposal as written plus its evidence paths, never the reasoning behind it. Dispatched agents and workflow steps never commit, push, publish or dispatch, and repo-maintainer acts only when the main session dispatched it on your request; one deliverable per agent; an agent idle past the overlay's limit, or stopped by a limit, is not resumed; when more work is needed, a fresh one starts from the files it left. The overlay's Runtime budget names your plan tier and any profile override; if the slot is missing, it asks you once and runs guarded meanwhile. Under guarded (free, pro, max and team plans) one isolated dispatch is in flight at a time and the conductor waits for its return; under open (ultra, enterprise, api) independent stages may run in parallel, the number following quality and the stages' dependencies, never speed; parallel stages touch disjoint files, each with its own tracker row. What comes back is a condensed return: its first line ACK RULES_HASH, then the verdict, counts, flagged items and the paths of the full outputs; the full report is written to a file and referenced by path, and the conductor reads it only for a flagged item, by line range, and answers a follow-up by reading it, not by re-dispatching; what is flagged is decided by the reviewer that wrote the report, never the conductor. On receipt the ACK line is checked first; a missing or stale one is a HARD-STOP for that return: a tracker row, said at the next checkpoint, then re-dispatch. Step 3: the stage's mechanical checks run as scripts; the conductor runs them and reads their summary. Step 4: the checkpoint is classified by the table and the tracker row is written. MANDATORY: at the stops the overlay names, at the position it names; you see the decision dashboard; it always waits, never skipped, never downgraded, never answered on your behalf. FULL: after 4 consecutive SLIM continues, the count resetting at every FULL or MANDATORY stop; after any failed gate; after any SOFT-GATE override; before any deviation from the pipeline of record, a stage skipped, reordered or added; you see the decision dashboard; it waits. SLIM: every other stage transition, the default; you see one line: stage done, check result, next stage, default; it does not wait, the default runs unless you stop it. The tracker is read at session start, holds one row per stage transition and is never deleted, a wrong row being superseded by a new one; a row holds date and time, unit, stage from and to, checkpoint class, gate result, override reason if any, and artifact references, paths and commit ids; memory may point at it, it never holds the state. Step 5: you are shown a SLIM line, or the decision dashboard, whose order is: key points, metrics against their targets, each number with its source, deliverables with paths, flagged items verbatim with their finding ids; a summary of at most 3 lines that never restates a finding; numbered options, one the default, which at a FULL or MANDATORY stop never runs without your reply; the self-check line: numbers, concession, trajectory, scope, completeness. Step 6: your choice, or the SLIM default, sends the next stage. A judgement turn is a hat switch: (conductor → role for this turn), that role's ACK line, that role's spec in full, (→ conductor); the worn role, not the conductor, owns what that turn produced. Judgement turns in between are worn roles (research-mentor, paper-writer, …), announced. The pipeline of record is the overlay's stage order, read at step 1: the Code / experiment or the Paper flow of core/roles/README.md; the project's own order is an overlay slot. Lane 1, Code / experiment: discuss (research-mentor), verify theory (math-reviewer), implement (dl-engineer), gate (regression-guardian), run (experiment-runner), analyze (results-analyst), commit (repo-maintainer). Lane 2, Paper: discuss research (research-mentor), pull numbers/figures (results-analyst), write/revise + compile (paper-writer), verify equations (math-reviewer), anonymize (tools/anonymize.py), independent critique (blind-reviewer), revise again (paper-writer), commit (repo-maintainer). Footnote, conductor hard rule 1: No substantive work. The conductor does not draft, revise, review, verify, analyze or rule on content.
svg.title: Scenario 1 — the whole thesis, run end to end from your session
svg.desc: You ask /conductor to run the thesis; it reads the tracker and the overlay's stage order, dispatches each stage across the context boundary with spec, hash and brief, reads the condensed return, runs the mechanical checks, classifies the checkpoint as MANDATORY, FULL or SLIM and writes the tracker row, shows you a SLIM line or the decision dashboard, and sends the next stage on your choice or the SLIM default. Judgement turns are worn roles, announced. Lane 1 and Lane 2 of the typical flows are the pipeline of record.
svg.text: The whole thesis, run end to end from your session
Read the tracker → dispatch the stage → condensed return → checks → checkpoint → your choice → next stage — the conductor does none of the stages' work.
